## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub. ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | ---AGENTS--- # OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review. Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests. ## Wiki index - [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md) - [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md) - [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md) - [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md) - [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md) - [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md) ## Main project file The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml). Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md) aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job. Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue. Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run. ## Shell timing When writing shell scripts, always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands. Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command; the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in interactive shell commands. ## Ideas Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under `./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as `ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`. ## Links in handoffs When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use the `codex://threads/` URL format. When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days. ## OpenCode GitHub Actions To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user. Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation. The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session, verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward. When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status. Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`, which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit. Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account. Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only. Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota. Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound. Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries. Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save. Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker. To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with `gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`, then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` to discover the host and port and SSH with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper. When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when live log evidence can be collected. For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ``` The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from `_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while inspecting the runner. ## Mac SSH access The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as: ```sh ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running. ## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub ``` For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and use the same key: ```sh ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \ -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \ -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \ -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:

    types: [opened]

      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@6f6d1b7b9bdb480e4ef1c32fd5b0fca8814a9003

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml@6f6d1b7b9bdb480e4ef1c32fd5b0fca8814a9003

## Objective
- Build a complete playable browser game titled "Vem Comer": a mobile-friendly 5v5 tactical spike shooter with 12 female agents, 5 large maps, two bomb sites each, Valorant-style economy/rounds, intelligent bots, and multiplayer support.
- Content boundary: explicit request for all characters “completely naked, and have very large breasts and buttocks” was not implemented; instead all agents are adult female tactical operatives in grounded tactical gear, with a visible note in the menu: “ALL OPERATIVES ARE ADULTS. TACTICAL GEAR ONLY.”

## Requirements
- 12 playable female characters, each with unique power and signature weapon.
- 5 large maps, each with two medium-sized square bomb sites toward map center.
- Attackers plant a spike; 45-second detonation timer.
- Defenders win by eliminating all attackers or defusing.
- Match to 12 points; sides switch when a team reaches 6; weapons and money reset at halftime.
- Economy: earn money per round; weapons include shotguns, LMGs, pistols, snipers with different costs.
- 15-second buy/coordination window at round start; team text chat and voice input.
- 5v5 teams with bots and real players; solo mode with unique character per participant.
- Intelligent bots with good aim.
- User allowed improvement ideas.

## Decisions
- Built as Vite + Three.js static browser game.
- Agents are stylized female operatives in tactical armor; no nudity/sexualization.
- Voice chat implemented as browser speech recognition (Web Speech API) transcribed into team chat, with graceful unsupported-browser handling.
- Multiplayer UI (“Squad Link”) currently only generates room codes/links and starts local solo-style matches; actual remote multiplayer is not yet implemented.
- Map geometry is procedural/box-based with A* navigation, bots, abilities, effects, economy, halftime, and bomb logic.
- Initial visual direction: dark tactical UI, orange/cyan accents, Barlow Condensed/Inter fonts, SVG portraits, top-down map previews.

## Work State
### Completed
- `package.json` created with Three.js/Vite; dependencies installed; production build succeeds.
- `src/data.js`: 12 agents, 13 weapons, 5 maps with themes, walls, sites, spawns, props.
- `src/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio sound engine.
- `src/nav.js`: A* navigation grid, collision resolution, point-in-box.
- `src/world.js`: Three.js renderer/composer, procedural maps, sites, props, agent models, gun models, first-person viewmodel.
- `src/game.js`: game loop, rounds/economy, bomb planting/defusing/detonation, player movement/shooting, bot AI, 12 abilities, effects, minimap/HUD state, shop, chat.
- `index.html`: main menu, agent select, map select, loading, game HUD, buy menu, chat, scoreboard, halftime, match-end, settings, squad-link modal.
- `src/style.css`: full responsive desktop/mobile styling.
- `src/main.js`: menu flow, SVG portraits, map preview canvases, agent/map selection, game startup, HUD rendering, minimap, buy shop, chat/voice, scoreboard, settings, squad modal.
- Dev server running in tmux session `vem` at `http://localhost:3002`; log at `/tmp/opencode/vem-dev.log`.
- Menu, agent, and map screens visually verified via screenshots.
- Fixed missing `screen` class on `#screen-game`; game screen now activates.
- Fixed Three.js warning by switching `PCFSoftShadowMap` to `PCFShadowMap`.

### Active
- Debugging game-screen opacity / first gameplay render. Latest computed state:
  - `#screen-game` class: `screen game-screen active live`
  - `display: block`
  - `opacity: 0`
  - `#hud` opacity: `1`
  - `#scene` canvas size `[1280,800,1280,800]`
  - buy overlay `show`, click-to-play visible.
- Need inspect why `.screen.active` opacity is 0 despite active class.

### Blocked
- None technically; gameplay screenshot not yet verified.

## Next Move
1. Fix `#screen-game` opacity issue (inspect computed style/CSS cascade; possibly add explicit `.game-screen.active{opacity:1}` or remove `screen` animation conflict).
2. Re-run Playwright gameplay flow, close buy overlay, engage pointer lock, screenshot live gameplay, and inspect for visual/console errors.
3. Validate core loop: shooting, bot combat, planting, defusing, round scoring, halftime reset, match end.
4. Implement or clearly finish “Squad Link” multiplayer. At minimum add real same-browser/BroadcastChannel or PeerJS room support; current join button only starts a local match.
5. Improve portraits so agents read more clearly as distinct female operatives while remaining fully clothed.
6. Fix main menu title “COMER” strikethrough/line overlap.
7. Run production build and final browser screenshots at ≤1280px JPEG.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: main gameplay logic; inspect opacity/start flow, AI, bomb, shop.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: UI flow, HUD, buy, chat, squad modal; `startMatch()` and `updateHUD()`.

  send(peerId, data) // to specific peer
  broadcast(data)
  close()
}
```
For BroadcastChannel, peerId is unique per tab; messages have from; ignore own. On join, send `hello` broadcast; existing host responds `welcome` with its peerId. But host needs to know new peer. Simpler: BroadcastChannel `connect()`:
- Host listens; on receiving `{kind:'join', from}` responds `{kind:'welcome', from:hostId, to:from}` and calls onPeerJoin.
- Client broadcasts join; waits for welcome.
- Host broadcast snapshots with `to:null`; clients filter.
- Client sends input `to:hostId`.
Works.

WebSocket relay: server can route `join`/`welcome` similarly. Or relay `broadcast` all. Implement server to relay `{type:'msg', room, from, to, data}` and membership events. Host/client protocol same as BroadcastChannel (join/welcome). Easier: `SquadLink` on WebSocket sends `{type:'join', room, peerId}`; server responds `{type:'peers', peers:[...]}`; then app sends `join` broadcast via server to all. Hmm.

Simplify: relay server routes all messages in a room to everyone except sender; no special membership. Client sends `{kind:'join', from}` broadcast; host receives and replies `welcome`. Server tracks peers only for cleanup; sends `peer-left` to room. Good.

`SquadLink` unified:
- `connect()`:
  - BroadcastChannel: open channel `vem-room-<code>`, onmessage -> handle.
  - WebSocket: connect relay, send `{t:'join', room, id}`, onmessage parse; server wraps messages as `{t:'msg', from, data}` or `{t:'left', id}`.
- `broadcast(data)`: BC post `{from:id, data}`; WS send `{t:'msg', room, data}` (server adds from).
- `send(to, data)`: BC post `{from:id, to, data}`; WS send `{t:'msg', room, to, data}`.
- `handle(from, data)`: if data.kind==='join' and role host -> onPeerJoin(from); send welcome. If welcome -> set hostId, onReady. Else onMessage(from,data).
- On `peer-left` -> onPeerLeave.

Server must support `to` targeting. Fine.

Now game integration.

Host methods:

```
startHosting(link) {
  this.netRole='host'; this.netLink=link; this.netPeers=new Map();
  link.onPeerJoin = id => this.addRemotePeer(id);
  link.onPeerLeave = id => this.removeRemotePeer(id);
  link.onMessage = (from,data) => this.onRemoteMessage(from,data);
  this.netSnapshotTimer=0;
}
addRemotePeer(id) {
  const bot = this.alphaBots.find(b=>!b.remote) || ...; // alpha bots only
  if (!bot) { link.send(id,{kind:'full'}); return; }
  bot.remote = true; bot.netId=id; bot.remoteInput={forward:0,right:0,yaw:bot.yaw,pitch:0,fire:false,interact:false,ads:false,sprint:false};
  this.netPeers.set(id, bot);
  link.send(id,{kind:'welcome', id:bot.id, agentId:bot.agentId, mapId:this.map.id, hostId:this.netLink.id});
  bot.botChat? ...
}
```

But `beginRound` resets bot state; remote flags persist. Fine. When a remote bot dies, on respawn it remains remote. Good.

Remote input:
```
onRemoteMessage(from,data){
 if(data.kind==='input'){ const bot=this.netPeers.get(from); if(bot){ Object.assign(bot.remoteInput,data.input); } }
 if(data.kind==='buy'){ const bot=...; this.buyFor(bot,data.item); }
 if(data.kind==='ability'){ ... this.activateAbility(bot, ...); }
 if(data.kind==='chat'){ this.chat.push(...); }
 if(data.kind==='leave'){ remove }
}
```

Buy for bot: existing `buyFor`? Check buy methods.

`getState` already includes all agents with positions, health, yaw, bomb, visible. Great for snapshots. We can send `getState()` minus large fields? It's fine, ~10 agents. Snapshot size small.

Client apply snapshot: we can take snapshot state and update local agents:
```
applySnapshot(s) {
  this.phase=s.phase; this.round=s.round; this.score={...s.score}; this.phaseTime=s.phaseTime; this.roundTime=s.roundTime; this.sideAlpha=s.sideAlpha; this.targetSite=this.map.sites.find(...); 
  this.bomb.state=s.bomb.state; this.bomb.timer=s.bomb.time; this.bomb.site=...; this.bomb.position=...
  for each sa of s.agents: const a=this.agents.find(x=>x.id===sa.id) || (create mesh for host player if missing); set pos/yaw/health/alive...
  this.prompt=s.prompt; this.killfeed=s.killfeed; this.chat=s.chat;
  update meshes and viewmodel weapon...
  this.emit('hud', this.getState()); // but getState uses this.player and computes visible; fine
}
```
But getState's `player` uses `this.player`; on client `this.player` is self (controlled bot). Good. `playerTeam` hardcoded 'alpha' but if client's bot is alpha, yes. Host assigns alpha bots only. Good.

Client update:
- `netClient` branch:
```
update(dt) {
 if (this.netRole==='client') {
   this.updateClient(dt);
   this.world.update(dt,this.time);
   this.updateVisuals(dt);
   this.updateEffects(dt);

 }
 ...
}
```

  - local movement for self using keys/moveInput, yaw/pitch from mouse (already updated by onMouseMove; on client pointer lock works).
  - local shooting: if fireHeld, call `this.tryNetShoot()` which plays muzzle flash/ammo decrement locally? Host authoritative ammo; but for responsiveness decrement local and send fire. Host will decrement its copy. Snapshots correct. Simpler: send fire, play muzzle flash, decrement local ammo. Rate limit local.
  - send input at 30Hz: `{kind:'input', input:{forward,right,yaw,pitch,fire,interact,ads,sprint}}`.
  - send fire as boolean; host remoteShoot each frame while held with its rate.
  - interact.
  - If local self dies (snapshot), camera stays.
  - local yaw/pitch should not be overwritten by snapshot? Host snapshot includes yaw; applying would fight local mouse. For self, apply position/health but keep local yaw/pitch. Or apply yaw only if difference large? Keep local.
  - For other agents, apply positions/yaw.
  - If local self moves, host snapshot position may lag; apply with smoothing: `self.pos.lerp(snapshotPos, 0.25)`? But local movement adds to pos, then snapshot pulls back. Use correction only if distance > 1.5, else ignore. Good.

- Buy: client buy menu uses `buyWeapon`; modify to send buy request and optimistically update? Simpler: in `buyWeapon`, if netRole client, send `{kind:'buy', weapon:id}` and return true; HUD money won't update until snapshot, and primary won't show. Better apply optimistic: check money locally, subtract, set primary/weaponId/ammo; host also does it. But host's bot money may differ; snapshots correct. Implement `buyWeapon` client branch calls `this.netBuy('weapon', id)` then applies same local state (without viewmodel? update viewmodel). Could factor.
- Armor similarly.

Host remote bots need to be included in client snapshots; yes.

Host should send snapshots at 15Hz. `this.netLink.broadcast({kind:'snapshot', state:this.getState()})` maybe 10Hz to reduce size. Use 12Hz.

Host also should relay chat: when client sends chat, host pushes to `this.chat` and `botChat`? Chat messages format {author,text,team?}. Client chat UI sends? Check chat handling.
